messages.author: 35cf403e5052bfe0
messages.subject: Reproducibility question
parts:
Hi All

I have been asked about how to get reproducibility with Nimble. I am not familiar with how setting seeds works in Nimble.

 

I assumed, following suggestions, that if you setSeed=number within the runMCMC function

then the results should be reproducible.

My question is ‘How close should the results be when the seed is the same for the same run?

 

Below is some results of running a spatial convolution model on some health data .  

I ran the following:

On R I set.seed= 123987001 and then ran the following

 

samples1<-runMCMC(CCONVMCMC,niter=niter,nburnin=10000,nchains=1,summary=TRUE,WAIC=TRUE,setSeed=123987001)

samples1$WAIC

samples2<-runMCMC(CCONVMCMC,niter=niter,nburnin=10000,nchains=1,summary=TRUE,WAIC=TRUE,setSeed=123987001)

samples2$WAIC

 

The results of these two calls were:

  1.  

samples1$WAIC

nimbleList object of type waicNimbleList

Field "WAIC":

[1] 318.6866

Field "lppd":

[1] -142.6599

Field "pWAIC":

[1] 16.68338

 

 

samples2$WAIC

nimbleList object of type waicNimbleList

Field "WAIC":

[1] 316.6697

Field "lppd":

[1] -142.3672

Field "pWAIC":

[1] 15.96761

The lppd is virtually the same but the variance penalty differs. There are also different numbers of warnings about pWAIC >0.4

 

 

Any suggestions about how to guarantee reproducibility or assurance that this is reproducibility welcome.

 

Best

Andrew

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Reproducibility question
parts:
Hi Andrew,
In theory setting the same seed should produce identical results. My first guess is that the model is not in identical state at the start of each run and that explains why the outputs are not identical. You could recreate the model state by doing something like the following, assuming Cmodel is the compiled model.

# before first run
savedVars <- list()
for(var in Cmodel$getVarNames()) {
 savedVars[[var]] <- Cmodel[[var]]
}

# before second run
for(var in Cmodel$getVarNames()) {
 Cmodel[[var]] <- savedVars[[var]]
}

HTH
Perry
